shortSummary: Subtropical evergreen soapberry tree treasured for jewel-red tuberculate fruits filled with translucent rose-scented aril flesh.
leadOverview: Lychee (Litchi chinensis)—called Lichu across Bengal—is an ornate broad-crowned subtropical fruit tree celebrated for hanging ruby-red fruit clusters harvested during Grishmo summer. Beneath its brittle pebbled crimson shell lies a glistening, pearl-white juicy aril perfumed with delicate floral monoterpenes and crisp sweet-acid balance.

sections.title: Morphological Description
sections.subtitle: Paripinnate glossy foliage, apetalous panicles, and crimson arillate fruits
sections.summary: Anatomy of dense domes, compound leaflets, apetalous flowers, tuberculate pericarps, and succulent white arils.
paragraphs: Litchi chinensis forms a handsome, symmetrically rounded evergreen crown 10 to 20 metres high with a short, furrowed grey-black trunk and brittle drooping branches. Leaves are alternate and evenly pinnate (paripinnate), bearing 4 to 8 glossy, leathery oblong-lanceolate leaflets that flush coppery-salmon before maturing to deep emerald above and glaucous pale green beneath.

Early spring produces erect terminal panicles up to 30 centimetres long bearing hundreds of tiny, greenish-white flowers lacking true petals (apetalous) but equipped with prominent fleshy nectar discs. The resulting fruit is botanically a one-seeded berry-like drupe encased inside a brittle, crimson-pink pericarp studded with rough hexagonal tubercles; inside surrounds a crisp, juicy translucent white aril clinging loosely around a glossy mahogany seed.

subblocks.heading: Crown & Bark
subblocks.text: Dense dome-shaped evergreen crown cast on dark grey furrowed trunks; young twigs brittle under high storm winds.

subblocks.heading: Paripinnate Leaflets
subblocks.text: 2–4 pairs of smooth leathery leaflets emerging vibrant pinkish-bronze to deter herbivores while developing chlorophyll.

subblocks.heading: Tuberculate Pericarp
subblocks.text: Leathery-brittle pink-to-scarlet rind etched with polygonal bumps that split cleanly at the longitudinal suture.

subblocks.heading: Translucent Aril
subblocks.text: Fleshy edible outgrowth of the seed funiculus rich in sugars, vitamin C, and geraniol floral esters.

sections.title: Taxonomy & Botanical Classification
sections.subtitle: Sapindaceae soapberry lineage alongside rambutan and longan
sections.summary: Taxonomic placement within Sapindaceae sharing fleshy edible arils and panicle nectaries.
paragraphs: Placed in order Sapindales and family Sapindaceae, Litchi chinensis is the sole widely cultivated species of genus Litchi—closely allied to longan (Dimocarpus longan, 'ashphal'), rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum), and soapnut (Sapindus).

Three botanical subspecies are recognized—most famously Litchi chinensis subsp. chinensis—selected over two millennia of Chinese and South Asian arboriculture into prized regional cultivars including Bombai, Bedana, China-3, Muzaffarpur, and Dinajpur's famed Madrajee.

sections.title: Natural Habitat & Global Distribution
sections.subtitle: Subtropical Pearl River valleys to Dinajpur and Ishwardi orchards
sections.summary: Ecological niche requiring cool winter chill followed by hot humid fruiting summers.
paragraphs: Indigenous to low-elevation humid forests of Guangdong and Fujian in southern China and northern Vietnam, lychee requires a very specific climatic rhythm: cool, dry winters (10–15°C) to induce flower panicles without frost damage, followed by warm humid summers during fruit enlargement.
In Bangladesh, this climatic sweet spot makes Dinajpur, Rajshahi, Pabna (Ishwardi), and Rangpur premier Lichu heartlands, where alluvial silt-loam terraces yield sweet harvests every Jyoishtho.

sections.title: Ecological Role & Pollinator Interactions
sections.subtitle: Obligate mycorrhizal roots, bee honey flows, and frugivorous bat dispersal
sections.summary: Dependence on arbuscular mycorrhizae, premier apiary nectar yields, and winged dispersal.
paragraphs: Lychee trees form obligate symbiotic partnerships with soil endomycorrhizal fungi—producing dense surface feeder roots coated with fungal hyphae that absorb phosphorus and zinc efficiently. Without these beneficial soil microbes, nursery air-layers struggle to establish.

During Boshonto bloom, exposed floral nectary discs attract immense swarms of Apis bees, producing pale amber monofloral 'Lichu honey' celebrated across northern Bangladesh. Later, fruit bats and civets disperse ripe red fruits.

sections.title: Economic, Culinary & Cultural Importance
sections.subtitle: Two millennia of orchard heritage, Lichu honey, and refreshing summer beverages
sections.summary: High-value seasonal fruit economics alongside floral apiculture.
paragraphs: Lychee boasts one of the longest unbroken written horticultural histories in the world—documented in Chinese imperial tributes dating back over 2,000 years. Today, fresh juicy Lichu defines the joyous short summer window across Bangladesh alongside mango and jackfruit.
Beyond fresh eating, chilled arils elevate fruit salads, sorbets, sparkling coolers, and floral patisserie creams, while pericarp anthocyanins and seed starches find uses in natural food dyeing.

sections.title: Traditional & Scientific Medicinal Properties
sections.subtitle: Oligonol polyphenols, vitamin C, and unripe hypoglycin A caution
sections.summary: Antioxidant epicatechin compounds in ripe pulp alongside strict warnings against unripe consumption on empty stomachs.
paragraphs: Ripe lychee arils deliver roughly 70 mg of vitamin C per 100 grams along with copper, potassium, and proanthocyanidin polyphenols (epicatechin and procyanidin A2)—studied for vascular antioxidant protection and post-exercise recovery.
In traditional Chinese herbalism, dried lychee seeds (Li Zhi He) and pericarps are used cautiously in regulated decoctions for mild digestive warming.
sections.safetyNote: Never consume unripe green lychees or eat large quantities of ripe fruit on an empty stomach, especially in malnourished children: unripe fruits contain elevated methylene cyclopropyl-glycine (MCPG) and hypoglycin A, which can block gluconeogenesis and trigger dangerous acute hypoglycemia.

sections.title: Comprehensive Cultivation & Care Guide
sections.subtitle: Air-layering over parent soil, windbreaks, and micronutrient zinc care
sections.summary: Sustaining fruitful orchards in acidic pH 5.5–6.8 loam inoculated with mycorrhizal topsoil.
paragraphs: Because lychee seeds remain viable for only 4 to 5 days after removal from fruit and rarely grow true to cultivar, orchards propagate almost exclusively via monsoon air-layering (guti kolom). When planting saplings in pH 5.5 to 6.8 well-drained humus loam, mix two spadefuls of soil from beneath a healthy mature lychee tree into the planting hole to introduce essential mycorrhizae.

Protect brittle young canopies with windbreak trees, withhold water during November–December to discourage winter leaf flush and induce flower buds, and mist trees with water or provide zinc-boron foliar sprays during scorching spring winds to prevent developing fruit skin cracking.

sections.title: Annual Phenology & Six-Season Rhythms
sections.subtitle: Flowering, fruiting, vegetative flush, and Shororitu synchrony
sections.summary: Seasonal cadence across Bengal's six-season cycle (Spring (বসন্ত), Summer (গ্রীষ্ম)).
paragraphs: Lychee (Litchi chinensis) aligns its vegetative flushes, anthesis, and fruit maturation tightly with Bengal's Shororitu photoperiod and monsoon moisture transitions, showing peak biological activity during Spring (বসন্ত), Summer (গ্রীষ্ম).

Spring (বসন্ত): Apetalous cream terminal panicles bloom across Dinajpur and Pabna, yielding prized spring Lichu honey. Summer (গ্রীষ্ম): Ruby-red tuberculate fruit clusters swell and ripen pearl-white arils during Jyoishtho heat.

sections.title: Seed Germination Biology & Propagation
sections.subtitle: Dormancy regulation, nursery media, and clonal propagation
sections.summary: Reproductive biology and reliable seed or vegetative propagation techniques for Lychee.
paragraphs: Lychee (Litchi chinensis) combines sexual seed propagation—useful for raising sturdy heterozygous rootstocks—with elite clonal techniques such as veneer grafting, air layering (gootee), and semi-hardwood stem cuttings. Fresh recalcitrant or semi-orthodox seeds typically germinate within 14 to 35 days when depulped and sown in warm organic loam.
Clonal orchards standardize crown architecture, early precocity, and uniform biochemical profiles across generations within Sapindaceae.

subblocks.heading: Nursery Seed Protocol
subblocks.text: Depulped seed sown cleanly in 2:1 loam-compost media; high viability when fresh.

subblocks.heading: Clonal Method
subblocks.text: Approach/veneer grafting or monsoon air-layering onto vigorous local rootstocks.

sections.title: Pathology Defense, Vectors & Organic IPM
sections.subtitle: Phytoalexin resilience, fungal prophylaxis, and predator guilds
sections.summary: Biochemical defense mechanisms and low-impact organic IPM guidelines for Litchi chinensis.
paragraphs: In humid South Asian and tropical growing belts, Lychee (Litchi chinensis) relies on secondary terpenoid resins, foliar trichomes, and phytoalexin phenolics as front-line biochemical deterrence against herbivores and opportunistic pathogens. Prolonged monsoon waterlogging or stagnant canopy humidity can nonetheless encourage anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.), powdery mildew, leaf-spot fungi, or root-zone Pythium.

Organic Integrated Pest Management (IPM) prioritizes preventive airflow pruning, Trichoderma-enriched compost amendments around feeder roots, and targeted cold-pressed Azadirachta indica (neem) oil sprays at dusk to suppress sap-sucking aphids, scale insects, and mealybugs without harming native pollinators.

subblocks.heading: Fungal Management
subblocks.text: Prevent overhead foliar wetness at dusk; maintain canopy aeration and copper/Trichoderma prophylaxis.

subblocks.heading: Organic Pest Control
subblocks.text: Neem kernel emulsion (3–5 ml/L) plus conservation of hoverfly and ladybird predator guilds.

sections.title: Conservation Standing & Climate Resilience
sections.subtitle: Population security, agroforestry corridors, and stress tolerance
sections.summary: Biogeographic conservation standing and climate adaptation traits of Lychee.
paragraphs: Across its native and naturalized distribution (Southern China, Northern Vietnam & Indo-Malayan Foothills), Lychee (Litchi chinensis) demonstrates strong ecological plasticity across alluvial floodplains, homestead agroforestry plots, and urban biodiversity corridors. While cultivated stands remain broadly secure, landrace genetic erosion, coastal salinity shifts, and wetland drainage threaten wild ecotypes and heritage regional varieties.

Long-term resilience depends on decentralized in-situ homestead stewardship, wetland buffer conservation, and botanical garden germplasm collections preserving drought-, flood-, and salinity-tolerant alleles amid shifting monsoon regimes.

subblocks.heading: Ecological Resilience
subblocks.text: Adapted to Southern China, Northern Vietnam & Indo-Malayan Foothills thermal oscillations and seasonal hydrological extremes.

subblocks.heading: Stewardship Strategy
subblocks.text: Preserve traditional landraces, pollinator corridors, and living herbarium voucher plots.

sections.title: Horticultural Spacing, Pruning & Telemetry
sections.subtitle: Plot geometry, canopy shaping, and calibrated soil-climate meters
sections.summary: Calibrated horticultural parameters: pH 5.5 – 6.8, Full Unobstructed Sun, and structural spacing guidance.
paragraphs: Optimal managed cultivation of Lychee (Litchi chinensis) calibrates root-zone chemistry around pH 5.5 – 6.8 inside deep humus-rich acidic loam. Providing adequate crown spacing prevents humidity buildup and lets lower shoots capture uniform irradiance across full unobstructed sun.

Light corrective pruning immediately after main flowering or harvest periods redirects assimilates into healthy vegetative framework, while moisture scheduling (moderate / seasonal dry rest) stabilizes root turgor without inducing hypoxia.

sections.title: Evolutionary Genetics & Adaptive Phylogeny
sections.subtitle: Sapindales clade divergence and Sapindaceae genomic traits
sections.summary: Phylogenetic placement of genus Litchi within order Sapindales (Eudicot (Malvids)).
paragraphs: Modern molecular phylogenetics (APG IV) places Litchi chinensis inside family Sapindaceae (স্যাপিন্ডাসি (লিচু গোত্র)), order Sapindales, clade Eudicot (Malvids). Subtropical soapberry trees producing pinnately compound foliage, terminal nectariferous panicles, and tuberculate fruits cradling juicy translucent edible arils.

Within genus Litchi, specialized morphological adaptations—such as evenly pinnate glossy foliage flushing coppery-salmon when young—reflect co-evolutionary specialization with regional pollinator guilds and abiotic habitat filters.

sections.title: Field Identification Key & Diagnostic Checks
sections.subtitle: Macro-morphological verification against look-alike taxa
sections.summary: Rapid field-sheet checklist for confirming Litchi chinensis (Lichu (লিচু)).
paragraphs: Field verification of Lychee (Litchi chinensis) rests on recognizing key Sapindaceae family markers: Evenly pinnate glossy foliage flushing coppery-salmon when young; Dense apetalous floral panicles featuring prominent honeybee nectary discs; Brittle pebbled pericarps enclosing a fleshy sweet aril around glossy seeds. Inspecting fresh leaf arrangement, stem surface texture, and reproductive architecture together eliminates confusion with sympatric congeners.
